title: Circular Non-Adjacent Max Sum
statement:
Pick values from a ring so that no two picked positions are neighbours, maximising the total.

Contract
- `values` is a non-null array of non-negative `int`s and may be empty. The positions form a circle: index `i` neighbours `i - 1` and `i + 1`, and the last index also neighbours index `0` (a single value has no neighbour to conflict with).
- Return the largest total of a set of pairwise non-neighbouring indices. Choosing nothing is allowed, so an empty array gives `0`.
- The total can exceed the `int` range, so return a `long`. Do not mutate `values`.

Examples
- `maxSum(new int[]{2, 3, 2})` returns `3`.
- `maxSum(new int[]{1, 2, 3, 1})` returns `4`.
- `maxSum(new int[]{6})` returns `6`.
hints: Ask which of the first and last positions can be used: they can never both be chosen.
Solve the straight-row version on two ranges that each leave out one end, then keep the better answer; mind arrays of length 0, 1 and 2.
Reuse a constant-space row routine over `[0, n-2]` and `[1, n-1]`. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space, where n is the array length.
inputSyntax: Input: the values in brackets or separated by spaces, for example: [1, 2, 3, 1]
